query: What recurring types of problems show up in these incident tickets?

per_column.name: problem_domain
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query about recurring problem types by categorizing tickets into meaningful domains. Values are well-grounded in short_description text: 'VPN connection issue'→connectivity, 'Cannot connect to database'→database, 'Email system not working'→email are all sound readings.

per_column.name: incident_scope
per_column.rationale: Provides a useful secondary grouping axis (system-wide vs individual vs departmental) to characterize problem patterns. However groundedness is weaker: 'WiFi connectivity issue in the sales department'→department_group and 'Marketing Department'→department_group are supported, but 'VPN connection issue'→individual_user and 'Email system not working properly'→individual_user assert a scope the terse text does not clearly state. The dominant 'system_wide' label (314) is often not derivable from short descriptions, suggesting some inference beyond evidence.

per_column.name: resolution_complexity
per_column.rationale: The concept of resolution type/complexity could aid analysis, but the values appear invented. The source samples contain only timestamps and a short_description with no resolution or work-notes text. Assigning 'infrastructure_change' to a VPN issue or 'server_restart' to a database connection issue is not warranted by any visible field; these are confident specifics the text is silent on. Strong hallucination signal.

judge.rationale: problem_domain is the strongest column and directly serves the query with well-grounded categorization. incident_scope adds a useful grouping axis but overreaches on many rows where scope isn't stated. resolution_complexity is the weakest: its values cannot be derived from the available fields (only timestamps and a short description are present) and read as fabricated resolution categories. Overall the added set is analytically useful but groundedness is dragged down by unsupported scope and resolution inferences.
